current_step_text: Use NEBcloner to identify restriction sites in your vector and insert, and to check buffer compatibility if doing a double digest. | Single digest: simple but can allow insert in both orientations — use if the insert is directional by sequence context, or if you will screen by colony PCR. | Double digest: two different enzymes giving incompatible ends force directional cloning — preferred when possible. Confirm both enzymes are active in the same buffer. Most NEB enzymes are compatible with CutSmart or rCutSmart. | Check for internal sites: confirm neither enzyme cuts within your insert or wit

Assemble on ice in order: water → buffer → DNA → enzyme(s) last. | Mix gently by pipetting (do NOT vortex); spin briefly. | Incubate at the enzyme-specific temperature (most NEB enzymes: 37.0 °C) for 60.0 min. Time-Saver enzymes (marked TS): 15.0 min is sufficient. | Stop reaction: heat-inactivate at 65.0 °C × 20.0 min (most HF enzymes) or 80.0 °C × 20.0 min — check the NEB datasheet. Alternatively add loading dye and proceed directly to gel.

Run the entire digest on a 0.8 % TAE agarose gel with a 1 kb ladder. | Confirm bands at expected sizes. Gel-extract both vector and insert — this removes uncut and partially-cut DNA, a major source of background colonies. Elute in 15.0 µL. Measure by NanoDrop. | Minimise UV exposure when excising bands — use long-wave UV (365 nm) or a blue-light transilluminator if available.

stage_name: 4 — Dephosphorylation of vector (recommended for single digests)
current_step_text: Why: after a single digest, the linearised vector can re-ligate on itself (background colonies with no insert). Removing the 5′ phosphate groups with a phosphatase prevents re-ligation — only the insert (which retains its 5′ phosphates) can close the circle. | Add 1.0 µL Quick CIP (NEB) or rSAP directly to the digested, gel-purified vector; incubate 37.0 °C × 10.0 min. | Heat-inactivate: 80.0 °C × 2.0 min (Quick CIP) or 65.0 °C × 5.0 min (rSAP). | Proceed directly to ligation — no additional cleanup needed after CIP/SAP inactivation.

Assemble on ice: water → 10.0 × T4 Ligase Buffer (thaw and vortex to dissolve ATP) → vector → insert → T4 DNA Ligase last. | Standard ligation: 16.0 °C × 16.0 h (overnight, cold room or PCR block). Good for difficult ligations (blunt ends, long fragments). | Quick Ligation (NEB M2200): 25.0 °C × 5.0 min. Convenient for routine sticky-end ligations. | Heat-inactivate at 65.0 °C × 10.0 min, then chill on ice. | Transform 2.0 µL into competent cells (see Transformation protocol).

Go to NCBI Gene and search for the gene of interest (e.g. "RBM39 human"). | Navigate to Genomic regions, transcripts, and products . | Click GenBank (top right) → Send to → File. Download the RefSeq entry (NM_XXXXX). | If unsure which is the canonical isoform, check UniProt for the canonical sequence annotation. | Open the GenBank file in SnapGene: untick all features → scroll to the first (or full-length) protein → mark the CDS region.

In SnapGene, navigate to your intended edit site (e.g. stop codon for C-terminal tag, start codon for N-terminal tag). | Select a ~200.0 bp region centred on the edit site — this will be your gRNA design template and donor context. | For N-terminal tags: target close to the start codon. For C-terminal tags: target just before the stop codon. Aim to cut as close to the insertion site as possible to maximise HDR efficiency.

Go to IDT CRISPR Cas9 Design Tool — paste your ~200.0 bp region. | IDT will return ranked gRNA candidates with on-target and off-target scores. Shortlist 2–3 candidates. | (Knock-in only) for each candidate, verify in SnapGene that silencing the PAM site (to prevent re-cutting after HDR) does not change the amino acid sequence — use synonymous substitutions whenever possible. | (Knock-out) target a constitutive exon shared across all relevant isoforms. Early exon frameshift indels are most reliable. Avoid exons subject to alternative splicing.

Start from the WT genomic sequence around the cut site. In SnapGene, introduce your modification (tag sequence, point mutation, etc.). | PAM silencing: mutate the PAM (NGG → NGA or similar) or the seed region of the protospacer (the ~12.0 bp proximal to PAM) to prevent Cas9 re-cutting the edited allele. Synonymous codon changes are preferred. | Keep the donor ≤200.0 bp total. Place your modification as close to the cut site as possible — HDR efficiency drops with distance from the DSB. | Typical design: ~50.0 bp homology arm — [tag/mutation] — ~50.0 bp homology arm. | Order as a standard desal

Plan controls before starting wet-lab work: untreated parental cells · mock electroporation (no RNP) · non-targeting guide . | Record guide IDs, donor version IDs, transcript choice, and reagent lot numbers before starting. | After the experiment: MiSeq amplicon sequencing is the definitive readout of editing outcome — plan your genotyping primers now (flanking the edit site, amplicon ~200.0 bp).

Design your 20.0 bp gRNA spacer targeting the gene of interest. Verify PAM (NGG, immediately 3′ of spacer) and assess on-target/off-target scores using Benchling or CRISPOR . | Design the ssOligo insert (≈ 70.0 nt total): 5′ homology arm (25.0 bp, matches PX458 upstream of the BbsI cut site) · 20.0 bp gRNA spacer · 3′ homology arm (25.0 bp, matches PX458 downstream of the BbsI cut site). | Order at 100.0 nmol scale (standard desalt purification is sufficient). | Upon receipt, resuspend in TE buffer + 50.0 mM NaCl to 100.0 µM stock; aliquot and freeze at -20.0 °C. | Prepare a 1.0 µM working sto

Digest 1.0 µg PX458 with BbsI (NEB) at 37.0 °C for 30.0 min following the manufacturer's protocol — see calculator below. | Confirm linearisation on a 1.0 % agarose gel (expected band ≈ 9.3 kb). | Excise the band and purify the linearised plasmid (NucleoSpin or equivalent). Measure concentration by NanoDrop — needed for the calculator below.

Set up the reaction on ice using the volumes from the calculator. Add components in order: water → vector → ssOligo → master mix. | Incubate at 50.0 °C for 60.0 min in a thermocycler (lid off or set to 55.0 °C). | Transform 2.0 µL into NEB Stable Competent E. coli (C3040H) — see the Transformation protocol; heat shock 42.0 °C × 30.0 s . | Plate on LB+ampicillin (100.0 µg/mL); pick 6–8 colonies; miniprep and verify by Sanger sequencing across the cloning site.
Plate 1 × 10⁶ wild-type cells per well in a 6-well plate . | Always include a negative control well (no transfection) seeded in parallel — used to set the GFP gate at FACS and confirm baseline.

Tube A — add 1.0 µg PX458-gRNA plasmid to 100.0 µL Opti-MEM . Mix gently. | Tube B — add 3.0 µL FugeneHD (Promega) to 100.0 µL Opti-MEM . Mix gently. | Combine Tube A + Tube B, mix gently, incubate 5.0 min at RT . | Add the entire complex dropwise to the well (no media change needed).

Incubate 24.0 h post-transfection — GFP (2A-fused to Cas9) needs this long to be expressed and mature before it's reliably detectable by flow cytometry. | Sort GFP-positive cells by FACS to enrich for Cas9-expressing transfected cells → proceed to Single Cell Sorting for clonal expansion.
tracrRNA: 20.0 nmol → 200.0 µL Nuclease-Free duplex buffer (IDT) → 100.0 µM stock . | crRNA: 2.0 nmol → 20.0 µL duplex buffer → 100.0 µM stock . | Spin down after reconstitution.
Add 50.0 µL reconstitution solution to lyophilized S. pyogenes Cas9 → 1.0 µg/µL. | Vortex gently, spin down, incubate 10.0 min on ice or overnight in fridge.
Add 5.0 µL of each (TracrRNA + crRNA) per tube (1 tube per crRNA). | Incubate at 95.0 °C × 5.0 min, then spin down.
Mix both components and incubate 20.0 min at RT.

Trypsinize, neutralize, wash with PBS, resuspend in 1.0 mL PBS. | Count: add 2×10⁵ cells/electroporation to Eppendorf. | Remove PBS by centrifugation. | Add 2.0 mL media to 6-well plate; seed same number of cells in negative control well.

Fill 50.0 mL falcon with ethanol, insert tips; aspirate and dry on paper; wash with PBS. | Add RNP mix to cell pellet; resuspend gently without generating bubbles. | Add 3.0 mL electrolyte solution to electroporation vessel. | Take 10.0 µL of mix with electroporating pipette → place in vessel → electroporate → dispense into well. Repeat per well. | Leave cells 48.0 h before analysis/sorting.

stage_name: After electroporation — pool validation (before single-cell sorting)
current_step_text: Maintain edited cells as a pooled population for 48.0 h minimum before analysis (allow NHEJ to resolve). | Check by MiSeq amplicon sequencing around the cut site — aim for >70.0 % frameshift indels before sorting. Optionally confirm loss of protein by western blot. | Define a go/no-go criterion before sorting (e.g. >70.0 % indels by MiSeq or a clean TIDE trace). If below threshold, consider re-electroporating with a different guide.

Design your 20.0 bp gRNA spacer . Verify PAM (NGG) and assess scores using Benchling or CRISPOR . | Design an ssOligo with: 5′ homology arm (25.0 bp) matching PX458 upstream of BbsI cut · gRNA spacer (20.0 bp) · 3′ homology arm (25.0 bp) matching PX458 downstream of BbsI cut. | Dissolve lyophilised ssOligo in nuclease-free water to 1.0 µM working stock .

Digest 1.0 µg PX458 with BbsI (NEB) at 37.0 °C for 30.0 min following the manufacturer's protocol — see calculator below. | Confirm linearisation on a 1.0 % agarose gel (expected band ≈ 9.3 kb). | Excise the band and purify the linearised plasmid (NucleoSpin or equivalent). Measure concentration by NanoDrop — needed for the calculator below.

Set up the reaction on ice using the volumes from the calculator. Add components in order: water → vector → ssOligo → master mix. | Incubate at 50.0 °C for 60.0 min in a thermocycler (lid off or 55.0 °C). | Transform 2.0 µL into NEB Stable E. coli (C3040H). Plate on LB + ampicillin (100.0 µg/mL) overnight 37.0 °C. | Pick 6–8 colonies; miniprep; verify by Sanger sequencing across the cloning junction.

Clone: Left HA (400.0 bp) — Insert — Right HA (400.0 bp) into a donor backbone. HAs must be perfectly homologous to the genomic locus. | Silence the PAM in the donor (1–2 silent mutations in the seed region) to prevent Cas9 from re-cutting after HDR. | Add a silent diagnostic SNP ~10.0 bp from the cut site to distinguish the HDR allele from WT by sequencing. | Zhang 2017 double-cut: design a second sgRNA on the opposite side of the insert; the two cuts release the insert+HAs from the circular plasmid. Use the same PX458 backbone or a separate gRNA plasmid. | Maxiprep both PX458 and donor (endo

Seed cells at 60.0 % confluency the day before in a 6-well plate or 10 cm dish. | Transfect: PX458 1.5 µg + plasmid donor 3.0 µg per well (ratio ~2.0–3 Cas9:donor). Use Lipofectamine 3000 per manufacturer protocol in Opti-MEM. | Incubate 24.0 h. Check GFP by fluorescence microscopy — expect 20.0 % GFP⁺ in transfectable lines. | Do not select with antibiotics during the first 48.0 h post-transfection.

48.0 h post-transfection: trypsinise, resuspend in sorting buffer (PBS + 2.0 % FBS + 10.0 mM HEPES, filter 0.22 µm). | Sort GFP⁺ cells (488 nm excitation). Gate top 10.0 % GFP⁺ for enrichment of Cas9-expressing cells. | Single-cell deposit into 96-well plates — see Single Cell Sorting protocol.

After 2–3 weeks expand colonies. Screen by junction PCR : one primer outside the HA, one inside the insert. A band indicates donor integration. | Sanger-sequence PCR product across both junctions (5′ and 3′) and the full insert. | Assess zygosity: run both junction PCRs + a WT-allele PCR. Heterozygous clones are common — confirm homozygosity by allele-specific sequencing or digital PCR. | Validate protein by Western blot, co-IP, or immunofluorescence before functional use.

Total length 100.0 nt . Flanking HAs of 40.0 nt each side of the edit. Asymmetric HAs (longer on the PAM-distal side) can improve HDR frequency. | Silence the PAM in the ssODN to prevent re-cutting. Introduce a silent diagnostic SNP ~10.0 bp from the cut site. | Order on the non-template strand (strand not used by Cas9 as template for nicking) — often gives higher HDR. | Standard desalted synthesis sufficient for ≤120.0 nt; PAGE-purify if >120.0 nt. Resuspend in TE pH 8.0 at 100.0 µM.

Resuspend crRNA and tracrRNA to 200.0 µM in nuclease-free IDT Duplex Buffer. | Mix equimolar crRNA + tracrRNA; anneal at 95.0 °C for 5.0 min, then cool slowly to RT in a heat block (turn off heater). Final gRNA duplex: 100.0 µM. | Mix gRNA duplex + Cas9 protein 1.0 by volume (e.g. 1.0 µL 61.0 µM Cas9 + 1.0 µL 100.0 µM gRNA) — used neat, no further dilution . Incubate 10.0 min at RT. | Add ssODN separately — do not pre-mix with RNP more than a few seconds before electroporation.

Harvest cells in log phase (70.0 % confluency). Viability must be >90.0 % before electroporation. | Pellet 1.0 ×10⁵ cells at 300 × g for 5.0 min. Wash once with PBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺). Remove all residual PBS. | Resuspend in electroporation buffer: Neon: Buffer R (10.0 µL tip) or Buffer T; 4D: SF or SE buffer (20.0 µL) per cell-line optimisation guide. | Add RNP ( 1.0 µL , ~100.0 pmol Cas9) + ssODN ( 1.0 µL , 100.0 pmol) to the cell suspension. Mix gently — do not vortex. | Neon parameters (HEK293T/HCT116): 1400–1500 V · 20 ms · 1 pulse. Optimise per cell type. 4D-Nucleofector: use manufactu

24.0 h post-electroporation: check viability and refresh medium. Expect 50.0 % viability. | 48.0 h: harvest a small aliquot for gDNA extraction. Run ICE analysis (Synthego) or T7E1 to confirm RNP activity — expect 20.0 % indels as proxy for cutting efficiency. | Single-cell sort or serially dilute into 96-well plates for clonal expansion — see Single Cell Sorting protocol.

Design PCR primers outside the ssODN HA region to avoid amplifying residual ssODN template. Expected amplicon 300.0 bp. | Run PCR product on gel to detect size difference (if insert ≥20.0 bp). Sequence all clones regardless. | Sanger-sequence to confirm the exact edit. Check both alleles — heterozygous clones are common with ssODN HDR. | Validate protein expression and function by Western blot and/or co-IP before use in experiments.

Grow T75 flasks to 60.0 % confluency in log phase; remove all media without disturbing cells. | Store in aliquots at 4.0 °C (few weeks) or -20.0 °C (long-term). | Before use: spin 4000.0 rpm × 5.0 min, discard pellet; filter through 0.22 µm filter. | Dilute 1.0 with 20.0 % FBS media (no antibiotics).
Aliquot 150.0 µL/well, leave at 37.0 °C, 5.0 % CO₂.
FACS media: 10.0 mL media + 100.0 µL FBS + 1.0 µL DAPI; filter through 0.22 µm.
Trypsinize, pellet, resuspend at 5×10⁶/mL in media + 1.0 % FBS (max 300.0 µL if <2.0 M cells).
Spin plates in TC room centrifuge (must tilt 90°). | Place at back of incubator 37.0 °C × ~20.0 days — do NOT touch .

After 20.0 days: mark wells with visible white specks; check all wells under microscope. | Add 50.0 µL fresh media to chosen wells; resuspend cells to disperse across well. | If contamination suspected: transfer full volume to new 96-well plate.

Optional: pre-cool centrifuge at 4.0 °C. | Prepare lysis buffer on ice: RIPA (~50.0 uL/6-well; ~50.0 uL/12-well) + 1.0 × PI (100.0 × stock) + benzonase (1000.0 ×). | Wash on ice: aspirate medium → cold PBS → aspirate PBS. | Add lysis buffer, distribute carefully; incubate 10.0 min in fridge (redistribute once). | Scratch down lysate (tilted plate); transfer to Eppendorf. | Optional: centrifuge 4.0 °C, 13,500 × g, 15.0 min; transfer supernatant. | Keep on ice for BCA or freeze at -80.0 °C.

BSA standards: 2, 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 mg/mL in ddH₂O — 25.0 uL per well, in duplicate. | Dilute lysates 6.0 (10.0 uL + 50.0 uL ddH₂O) or 10.0 for concentrated samples. | Load 25.0 uL standard + sample in duplicate; add 200.0 uL BCA reagent (50:1 A:B); mix 600.0 rpm × 1.0 min; 37.0 °C × 30.0 min. | Remove bubbles with a needle; read at 562 nm; confirm R² ≥ 0.99. | Use the BCA & Sample Prep protocol's calculator to convert BCA concentrations into loading volumes.

Running buffer: 1.0 × MOPS from 20.0 × stock (1.0 L). | NuPAGE 4.0 % bis-tris pre-cast gel: remove white strip; remove comb after assembling; fill with running buffer; wells facing inwards. | Load ladder (2.5 uL); run 180 V × 1.0 h 15.0 min (20-well gel).

Cut nitrocellulose membrane + Whatman filter paper to 7.0 ×9 cm; pre-wet sponges and filter paper. | Assemble sandwich (black to black); run 90 V × 90.0 min in ice-cold tank. | Ponceau × 1.0 min rocking; rinse with tap water; confirm even loading. | Wash TBS-T × 5.0 min; block 5.0 % milk TBS-T × 1.0 h RT; rinse TBS-T × 5.0 s. | Primary antibody in 5.0 % milk TBS-T overnight at 4.0 °C; keep antibody for reuse (freeze).
Wash 2.0 × TBS-T × 5.0 min. | Secondary: α-Ms/Rb (4000.0) + α-tubulin hFAB rhodamine (4000.0) in TBS-T; 1.0 h RT on rocker. | Wash 3.0 × TBS-T × 5.0 min; image.
Seed one 10 cm plate per condition: 1.2 M cells/plate. | Optional: seed extra plate/condition for MS analysis. | Treat cells; start with 1.0 h compound incubation.

Wash with PBS; add RIPA (300.0 µL/well) + 1.0 × PI (100.0 ×) + benzonase (1000.0 ×). | Incubate 10.0 min in fridge; redistribute once. | Scrape, transfer to Eppendorf; centrifuge 13000.0 rpm × 15.0 min; keep supernatant. | BCA quantification; normalize to ~3.0 mg/sample.

200.0 µg sample → split: 100.0 µg INPUT + 100.0 µg IP. | IP lysate → 2 tubes: Tube 1 — RBM39 IgG (2.0 µg/250.0 µg protein; 40.0 µL/mg if at 200.0 µg/mL); Tube 2 — Ms IgG control (1.0 µg/mg lysate). | Add RIPA to 1.0 mL total; incubate overnight 4.0 °C with rotation.

Wash Protein G/A beads (25.0 µL/sample): 500.0 µL wash buffer (50.0 mM Tris + 150.0 mM NaCl) × 2, magnetic rack. | Add overnight samples to beads; incubate 1.0 h 4.0 °C with rotation. | Collect flow-through on magnetic rack (keep for analysis). | Wash 5.0 × with 1000.0 µL wash buffer.
Add 80.0 µL loading buffer (4.0 × LDS + 10.0 × DTT); boil 90.0 °C × 10.0 min; collect supernatant on magnet. | Run on SDS gel → western blot.

Separate proteins by SDS-PAGE (include prestained MW markers). | Transfer to nitrocellulose membrane (iBlot or wet transfer). | Rinse membrane in TBS-T (removes transfer buffer; solubilizes HiBiT tag); keep in TBS-T or water until step 6. | Prepare Nano-Glo® HiBiT reagent: dilute 10.0 × Nano-Glo® Blotting Buffer in water → add LgBiT (200.0 ×) → add Nano-Glo® Luciferase Substrate (500.0 ×). | Incubate membrane × 5.0 min with gentle rocking. | Image with chemiluminescence imager — keep membrane in solution for continuous binding.

Plate HEK293FT at 1.5×10⁵ cells/mL in 10.0 mL into 10 cm dish. | Next day (~60.0 % confluency): prepare transfection mix — pick the Gag-Pol plasmid that matches your vector (see note above): Tube 1: 300.0 µL OptiMEM + 6.0 µg vector plasmid ( pBabe/pRetroX for retroviral, or your lentiviral transfer plasmid) + 3.8 µg Gag-Pol ( Retro-X GAG-POL for retroviral · Lenti-X GAG-POL for lentiviral) + 2.0 µg VSV-G (same reagent, either system) Tube 2: 300.0 µL OptiMEM + 24.0 µL PEI | Incubate 5.0 min in hood; combine tubes, mix gently, incubate 20.0 min. | Add to 9.0 mL pre-warmed complete media; mix ge
Remove media; centrifuge 2100 × g × 5.0 min; filter through 0.45 µm; use or store at -80.0 °C.

Seed 3 wells per plasmid in 6-well plate overnight (0.5 M cells/well, 2.0 mL media). | Prepare 3 media tubes: (a) virus only, (b) virus:media 1.0, (c) media only. | Add Polybrene to 8.0 µg/mL (1.6 µL/2.0 mL); add to each well; incubate ~24.0 h. | Replace with selection antibiotic at 48.0 h post-transduction. | Recover after selection; expand; after 3 passages, transfer to CL1 incubators.
DTT vial (7.7 mg) + 100.0 µL H₂O → 500.0 mM stock; add volume for 20.0 mM final in each tube. | Incubate 55.0 °C × 20.0 min.
200.0 mM TEAB from 1.0 M stock; add 132.0 µL to alkylator vial → 375.0 mM; add for 20.0 mM final. | Incubate 10.0 min RT in the dark (cover tubes).
Add 10.0 of 12.0 % phosphoric acid (e.g. 5.0 µL to 45.0 µL sample).

Binding/Wash buffer: 1.0 mL TEAB 1.0 M + 9.0 mL MeOH (100.0 mM TEAB in 90.0 % MeOH). | Add 7.0 × sample volume of buffer; mix; transfer entirely to S-Trap in 1.5 mL tube. | Centrifuge 4000 × g × 30.0 s; if not fully passed through, centrifuge again (up to 15,000 × g for clogs).
Add 150.0 µL Binding/Wash buffer; centrifuge 4000 × g × 30.0 s; discard flow-through; repeat ×3. | Final centrifuge 4000 × g × 1.0 min; transfer S-Trap to fresh tube.

Ratio 15.0 (recommended): 100.0 µg protein → 6.67 µg trypsin; mix 100.0 µg trypsin in 1500.0 µL 100.0 mM TEAB → add 100.0 µL to each S-Trap. | Spin to pass trypsin through; recover and add back. | Cap loosely — do NOT seal airtight (pressure forces solution out). | Incubate 37.0 °C overnight.

100.0 µL 50.0 mM TEAB → 4000 × g × 1.0 min. | 100.0 µL 0.15 % formic acid → 4000 × g × 1.0 min. | 100.0 µL 50.0 % ACN → 4000 × g × 1.0 min. | Transfer all to labelled tubes; take ~30.0 µg/sample; dry in SpeedVac (Proteomics bay).

Create a new folder inside the RAW data directory for this experiment (e.g. Samples_1-20_COMPOUND_DATE ). | All DIA-NN outputs and downstream analyses must live in this folder. | Write down your sample order before opening DIA-NN — you will need it for Perseus annotation.

Use the human whole-proteome FASTA available on the computer room workstation (contaminants already added). | If you have custom sequences to detect (knock-in tags, HiBiT, fluorescent proteins, exogenous constructs): open the FASTA in a text editor and add them manually in standard FASTA format: >sp|CUSTOM|MY_TAG_HUMAN MGSSHHHHHH... | Why this matters: DIA-NN generates in silico tryptic peptides from this file and matches experimental MS2 spectra against them. Any protein not in the FASTA will not be quantified, regardless of how many peptides you have for it.

Load raw files: top left panel → RAW → Select all → Open (all .raw or .mzML files for this experiment). | Add FASTA: click "Add FASTA" → select your prepared FASTA file. | Library generation: enable "FASTA digest for library-free search" — generates the spectral library on the fly from your FASTA. Enable deep learning-based spectra and RT prediction . | General settings: leave all defaults unchanged. | MBR (Match Between Runs): ✅ ENABLE — uses retention time alignment to transfer identifications between runs, dramatically improving quantitative completeness, especially for low-abundance protei

report.pg_matrix.tsv — main output : protein group quantification matrix. This is what you load into Perseus. | report.tsv — precursor-level report, more granular, useful for troubleshooting. | report.stats.tsv — per-run QC stats: number of proteins identified, median CV, etc. Check this first to spot problematic runs before statistical analysis.

Top left → Generic matrix upload . | Select report.pg_matrix.tsv from your DIA-NN output folder. | Text format is auto-detected — confirm. | Select all sample columns → assign to "Main" (these are your quantitative intensity values). | Click OK → Save As immediately (File → Save As) with a descriptive name. Do this before any processing.

Go to Annotation rows (top menu). | Add categorical annotation → assign group labels per sample column (e.g. Samples 1–4 → "Compound_1", Samples 5–8 → "DMSO"). | Why this matters: Perseus uses these group labels to define comparisons in the volcano plot and t-test. Mislabelling here means wrong statistics — double-check against your sample list from DIA-NN. | Tick the checkbox → OK.

Top left → Basic → apply log₂ transform to all Main columns. | Why: raw intensity values span many orders of magnitude and are not normally distributed. Log₂ transformation compresses the range, making distributions more symmetric — required for t-tests and PCA to be valid. A 1-unit change in log₂ = 2-fold change in abundance.

stage_name: D — Filter contaminants and low-quality IDs
current_step_text: Processing → Filter rows → Filter rows based on categorical column . | Remove Reverse (+) — decoy/reverse-sequence hits, not real protein IDs. | Remove Only identified by site (+) — lower-confidence identifications supported only by modified peptides. | Remove Contaminants (+) — common sample prep contaminants (keratins, trypsin, albumin…). | Note: if loading DIA-NN output directly, these columns may not exist — skip this step if absent.

Processing → Filter rows → Filter rows based on valid values . | Recommended setting: minimum 2 valid values in at least one group — keeps proteins quantified in at least one condition, even if missing in the other. | Avoid requiring valid values in all groups — this discards many real hits genuinely absent in one condition (e.g. degraded proteins). | Optional: additionally filter by Peptides > 2.

Top left → Imputation → replace missing values from normal distribution. | Leave default settings (downshift = 1.8, width = 0.3) → OK. | Why impute? Statistical tests require complete matrices. Proteins missing in one condition but quantified in another are real biological signals — imputing from the low end of the distribution allows these to appear as significant hits in the volcano plot.

stage_name: G — Exploratory analysis: PCA (optional but recommended)
current_step_text: Top middle → Principal Component Analysis . | Replicates should cluster tightly together; different conditions should separate. | An outlier replicate that clusters away from its group signals a problem (failed sample prep, labelling error, degraded sample) — consider excluding it and re-running.

Top middle → Volcano Plot . | Define comparison: e.g. "Compound_1" vs "DMSO" using your categorical annotation. | Settings: t-test type = Student's t-test ; FDR = 0.05 ; S0 = 0.1 (controls curve shape — increase to be more stringent). | Proteins in the upper right (enriched) or upper left (depleted/degraded) above the significance curve are your hits.

Right-click any protein in the volcano → Export → Plain matrix . | Save as .txt; open in Excel for further annotation. | Also export the full processed matrix: File → Export → Generic matrix export → .txt.

Design amplicon-specific primers around site of interest; optimal amplicon ~200.0 bp (excl. universal tag); site should be central in the amplicon. | Avoid non-coding regions (higher SNP density). | Tool: NCBI Primer-Blast (~300.0 bp template, set range so site is central). | Add Illumina Nextera XT overhangs: Fwd: TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + your primer Rev: GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG + your primer | Optional: test for dimers/hairpins with IDT OligoAnalyzer . | Order as standard desalted; reconstitute to 100.0 µM stock, working at 10.0 µM.
Run 10.0 µL on 1.0 % TAE agarose gel — expect 267.0 bp for 200.0 bp amplicon.
Set up 2 replicate reactions per sample; pool afterwards. | Run 10.0 µL on 1.0 % TAE agarose gel to confirm single band.

Equilibrate beads to RT; vortex 10.0 s; add 0.8:1 bead:sample ratio. | Incubate RT × 8.0 min; magnetic separator × 5.0 min; remove supernatant. | Add 200.0 µL fresh 80.0 % EtOH × 2 washes (30.0 s each on magnet); remove EtOH. | Air dry until shiny disappears but before cracks appear; add 30.0 µL molecular-grade H₂O; incubate 2.0 min RT; transfer supernatant.
Check concentration: NanoDrop or Qubit. | Submit ≥6.0 µL at 15.0 ng/µL; label: name + date + "For MiSeq".

Donor: Tb-labelled antibody or nanobody against tag on E3 ligase subunit (e.g. Tb-anti-His against His₆-CRBN-DDB1). Emission measured at 490 nm (Tb) and 520 nm (acceptor). Ratio = 10000.0 × (520 nm / 490 nm) = ratiometric TR-FRET unit (RTU). | Acceptor: fluorophore-labelled antibody against tag on POI (e.g. AF488-anti-GST against GST-BRD4). Must have good spectral overlap with Tb emission. | Bell-shaped curve: at low [PROTAC], ternary complex increases (rising phase); at high [PROTAC], binary complexes dominate and displace ternary (hook effect / falling phase).
